title: What If Earth Stopped Spinning?
premise: A scientifically careful anime What If: if solid Earth stopped rotating instantly, air and water would retain momentum; if the planet then continued orbiting the Sun, a solar day would last about a year.

shots.what: Glide through a layered anime dusk city as traffic light trails echo the equator moving east.

narration.text: At the equator, Earth moves east at about sixteen hundred seventy kilometers an hour.

sfx.name: soft-whoosh
sfx.prompt: A soft cinematic airy whoosh, quiet under narration.

shots.what: An ornate anime clock accelerates, freezes, and transitions to a clean equator speed graphic.

narration.text: We do not feel the spin; the ground, air and oceans travel with us.

sfx.name: clock-freeze
sfx.prompt: A delicate clock tick that stops with a tiny soft shimmer.

shots.what: The city ground locks in place while airborne leaves and cloud wisps continue east, clearly marked as a thought experiment.

narration.text: Imagine the solid ground stops instantly. It is a thought experiment; no known process can halt Earth that way.

sfx.name: soft-impact
sfx.prompt: A restrained low cinematic impact, brief and quiet under the voice.

shots.what: Camera follows loose paper and atmospheric ribbons past curved, detailed anime architecture without claiming a specific wind speed.

narration.text: The air and loose objects keep moving. The mismatch is greatest near the equator.

sfx.name: wind-swish
sfx.prompt: A soft broad wind pass, low in the mix under narration.

shots.what: A sculpted moonlit ocean swells toward a detailed coastal city; keep flooding conditional on how rotation stops.

narration.text: The oceans carry momentum too. Water would surge, but exact flooding depends on how the stop happens.

sfx.name: wave-swell
sfx.prompt: A gentle cinematic ocean swell, no sharp crash, quiet under narration.

shots.what: A beautifully lit, stationary Earth sits against a moving Sun; the terminator advances slowly to represent the year-long solar day.

narration.text: If Earth stopped spinning but kept orbiting the Sun, one solar day would last about a year.
That means months of daylight, then months of night. Winds and ocean circulation would change.

sfx.name: space-glimmer
sfx.prompt: A small soft glassy shimmer as Earth appears, not a loud impact.

shots.what: Pull back from the globe into a luminous starfield as the concise science takeaway appears in calm lettering.

narration.text: Climate needs models; spin shapes winds and oceans.

sfx.name: closing-air
sfx.prompt: A subtle airy resolve that leaves room for the final narration.
